\section{Gaussian Space --- Normalized Sums}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.NormalizedSums
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Normalized Sums: Introduction}
The multilinear polynomial for a normalized sum has degree one, equal coordinate influences, and unit variance in positive dimension. Moment-matched independent inputs admit quantitative Gaussian comparison against Lipschitz tests.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Normalized Sums: Results}

\begin{definition}[Normalized-sum multilinear polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedSumPolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
For $n\ge0$, define a multilinear coefficient family $P_n$ on subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ by $P_n(S)=1/\sqrt n$ when $|S|=1$ and $P_n(S)=0$ otherwise; division by zero is zero. Its evaluation is $n^{-1/2}\sum_i z_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Degree bound for the normalized-sum polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedSumPolynomial_hasDegreeAtMost}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedSumPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost}
\difficulty{1}
For every nonnegative integer $n$, the multilinear coefficient family whose coefficient
is $1/\sqrt n$ on singleton subsets and zero on all other subsets has degree at most
one; here division by zero is interpreted as zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Influence of a Normalized-Sum Polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.influence_normalizedSumPolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedSumPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.fourierCoeff_eval, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.influence_eq_sum_fourier}
\difficulty{5}
For a natural number $n$ and a coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $P_n$ be the
multilinear coefficient family equal to $1/\sqrt n$ on singleton subsets and zero on all
other subsets, and evaluate it on the Boolean cube using the Walsh characters. The
influence of coordinate $i$ in this evaluated function is $1/n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Variance of the normalized sum on the Boolean cube]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.cubeVariance_normalizedSumPolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.influence_normalizedSumPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedSumPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_eq_sum_nonempty_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.fourierCoeff_eval, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and on the uniform Boolean cube $\{0,1\}^n$ define
$f(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n(-1)^{x_i}$. Then $\operatorname{Var}(f)=1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Evaluation of the normalized sum polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.evalMultilinearRV_normalizedSumPolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedSumPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\Omega$ be a measurable space, and let $X_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be
arbitrary functions for $i=0,\ldots,n-1$. For every $\omega\in\Omega$, the multilinear
polynomial whose singleton coefficients are $1/\sqrt n$ and whose other coefficients are
zero evaluates to $\bigl(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}X_i(\omega)\bigr)/\sqrt n$, with the usual real
division convention when $n=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian comparison for normalized sums]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedSum_lipschitz_comparison}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.cubeVariance_normalizedSumPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.evalMultilinearRV_normalizedSumPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasInvarianceMoments_gaussianCoordinate, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.influence_normalizedSumPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_lipschitz, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianProjection, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedSumPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedSumPolynomial_hasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{6}
There is a constant $K>0$ such that the following holds. Let $n$ be a positive integer,
let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent real
random variables on it, each satisfying the fourth-order invariance moment conditions:
finite fourth absolute moment, mean zero, second moment one, third moment zero, and
fourth moment at most $9$. For any $c\ge 0$ and any $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi:\mathbb
R\to\mathbb R$, the difference between the expectation of $\psi(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n
X_i)$ and its expectation under the standard Gaussian measure has absolute value at most
$Kc n^{-1/4}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform cube expectation as product integration]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_uniformBool_pi_eq_expect}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.moment_eq_expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{4}
For every integer $n\ge0$ and every function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, its integral
against the product of $n$ uniform probability measures on $\{0,1\}$ equals its uniform
cube expectation $2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian comparison for normalized Boolean sums]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolSum_lipschitz_comparison}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasInvarianceMoments_uniformBoolCoordinate, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedSum_lipschitz_comparison, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{5}
There exists a constant $K>0$ such that for every positive integer $n$, every $c\geq0$,
and every $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the uniform average
of $\psi(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\sigma(x_i))$ over Boolean vectors
$x\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}^n$ differs from its integral under the standard
Gaussian probability measure $\gamma$ by at most $Kc(1/n)^{1/4}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian limit for normalized Boolean sums]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_normalizedBoolSum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolSum_lipschitz_comparison, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{pdf-681b6f3d947f-p018-b002}
\difficulty{5}
For every $c\ge0$ and $c$-Lipschitz $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, if $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_{m+1}$ are independent uniform signs and $Z$ is standard Gaussian, then $\mathbb E\psi((m+1)^{-1/2}\sum_i\epsilon_i)\to\mathbb E\psi(Z)$ as $m\to\infty$, where the first expectation is integration under the product sign law.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian limit for Lipschitz functions of cube sums]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_expect_normalizedBoolSum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_uniformBool_pi_eq_expect, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_normalizedBoolSum, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c\ge0$ and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $c$-Lipschitz. For each positive
integer $m$, choose a uniformly random vector $X\in\{0,1\}^{m+1}$ and encode each
coordinate by $1$ for $0$ and $-1$ for $1$. The expectation of $\psi$ applied to the sum
of these signs divided by $\sqrt{m+1}$ tends, as $m\to\infty$, to the expectation of
$\psi$ under the standard Gaussian probability measure on $\mathbb R$.
\end{lemma}
